_source: Ridgeline Metal clone, financial analysis as stored by the 2026-09-26 acceptance run (acc-data-cim/fa.json, fa-disc.json)

notes: Adjusted EBITDA calculation: Net income + Amortization + Interest + Taxes + One-time expenses (crane rebuild, legal fees, Silverthorn bad debt excess) + Discretionary expenses (Donna salary above market, owner's truck & personal, hockey sponsorship).

SDE calculation: Adjusted EBITDA + Owner's full compensation (management salary $180,000). The market salary of $165,000 is already included in adjusted EBITDA (only the $15,000 excess is added back), so SDE = Adjusted EBITDA + $165,000.
Check: the note above states 2024 adjusted EBITDA as $1,537,000; the add-backs listed here compute $1,552,000.
2024 SDE: $1,537,000 (adjusted EBITDA) + $165,000 (market GM salary) = $1,702,000.
Check: the note above states 2024 SDE as $1,702,000; the add-backs listed here compute $1,717,000.

Seller's claimed adjusted EBITDA of 'close to 1.8' ($1,800,000) includes the owner's full $180,000 salary, which is only partially an add-back to adjusted EBITDA ($15,000 above market). The seller's figure is closer to SDE ($1,702,000) than adjusted EBITDA ($1,537,000).
Dividends: Class D dividends of $60,000 paid in 2024 (and 2023) are distributions of after-tax profit from retained earnings. They do not appear on the P&L and are not add-backs to EBITDA or SDE.

Owner's total compensation: The seller's add-back list claims $260,000 total owner compensation, which appears to include salary ($180,000 T4) + dividends ($60,000 T5) + personal expenses ($28,000) = $268,000. However, only the salary ($180,000) is an expense on the P&L and thus an add-back. Dividends are not an add-back. Personal expenses ($28,000) are a separate discretionary add-back.

Market salary estimate: A general manager for a $10M industrial fabrication shop in Alberta with 42 employees, CWB Division 2 certification, and customer relationship management responsibilities would command approximately $165,000 in total compensation (base salary + benefits). This is a conservative estimate; some buyers may use a lower replacement cost.

Donna McAllister: Paid $62,000 in 2024 for part-time bookkeeping (office management per T4 summary). Market rate for a part-time bookkeeper in Leduc/Nisku area is estimated at $45,000. The $17,000 excess is treated as a discretionary add-back (family member above-market compensation).

One-time expenses: Crane rebuild ($64,000) and legal fees for shareholder agreement amendment ($18,000) are clearly one-time and supported by financial statements. Seller states crane rebuild won't recur for 20 years.

Discretionary expenses: Hockey sponsorship ($12,000) and owner's truck & personal expenses ($28,000) are discretionary and supported by seller's add-back list. These are typical owner perks in a closely-held business.

Bad debts: The 2022 bad debt of $22,000 (Silverthorn Energy receivership) is significantly higher than 2023 ($9,000) and 2024 ($12,000). The excess of $11,500 above the average of $10,500 is treated as non-recurring. Ongoing bad debt expense of approximately $10,000-$12,000 per year is normal for this business.
Interest expense: Declining from $79,000 in 2021 to $58,000 in 2024 as long-term debt is paid down. A buyer may have different financing costs.

Taxes: Current income taxes on taxes payable method. CCA claimed for tax purposes exceeds book amortization in all years, creating a timing difference but no deferred tax liability is recorded (compilation engagement).
Growth trajectory: Adjusted EBITDA has grown from $875,000 in 2021 to $1,537,000 in 2024 (76% growth over 3 years), driven by revenue growth (29% over same period) and improving margins.
Margin analysis: Adjusted EBITDA margin improved from 11.4% in 2021 to 15.7% in 2024. SDE margin improved from 13.5% in 2021 to 17.3% in 2024.
Working capital: The business generates strong operating cash flow ($1,132,410 in 2024) and has minimal working capital requirements relative to revenue. Cash conversion is excellent.

Buyer considerations: A buyer may have different financing costs (interest), tax rates, and depreciation schedules. A buyer may also have different discretionary expenses (no hockey sponsorship, different vehicle policy). The normalized EBITDA and SDE figures provide a baseline for valuation and comparison.

Income Statement net income now ties to the reported net income used here (Owner's truck & personal expenses, Hockey sponsorship (Leduc junior team, discretionary) counted as expenses again on the Income Statement).

addbacks.label: Owner compensation (President — Gord McAllister)
addbacks.description: Owner's pay $180,000 (2024) less a $165,000 market salary for the role: the difference counts for EBITDA and SDE; the market salary is added back for SDE only. Management salary paid to majority shareholder Gord McAllister per T4. A general manager for this role would cost approximately $165,000 (market salary for operations-focused GM in Alberta industrial fabrication sector).

addbacks.label: Owner compensation (President — Gord McAllister) — market salary
addbacks.description: SDE adds back the owner's full pay; this is the market-salary part. A buyer who hires someone for the role pays it, so it is not added back to EBITDA.

addbacks.label: Donna McAllister salary above market (bookkeeper)
addbacks.description: Donna McAllister (owner's wife) paid $62,000 in 2024 ($58,000 in 2023) for part-time bookkeeping. Market rate for part-time bookkeeper estimated at $45,000. Excess above market: $17,000 in 2024, $13,000 in 2023.

addbacks.label: Owner's truck & personal expenses
addbacks.description: Owner's truck on company (fuel, insurance), personal meals, cell phone, season tickets. Per seller's add-back list.

addbacks.label: Crane rebuild (both 10-ton cranes, one-time)
addbacks.description: Rebuild of both 10-ton overhead cranes in summer 2024: new hoists, end trucks, pendants. Deducted as current expense. Won't recur for 20 years per seller.

addbacks.label: Legal fees — shareholder agreement amendment (one-time)
addbacks.description: Legal fees for unanimous shareholder agreement amendment in November 2024 to facilitate sale. One-time expense.

addbacks.label: Hockey sponsorship (Leduc junior team, discretionary)
addbacks.description: Discretionary sponsorship of Leduc junior hockey team. Per seller's add-back list.

addbacks.label: Amortization of property and equipment
addbacks.description: Non-cash depreciation expense. Book amortization differs from CCA claimed for tax purposes.

addbacks.label: Interest on long-term debt
addbacks.description: Interest expense on equipment term loan and vehicle/equipment loans. Declining as debt is paid down.

addbacks.label: Income taxes — current
addbacks.description: Current income taxes on taxes payable method (no deferred taxes recorded). CCA exceeds book amortization in all years.

addbacks.label: Silverthorn Energy receivership bad debt (one-time)
addbacks.description: 2022 bad debt of $22,000 was single customer (Silverthorn Energy Services) which went into receivership in September 2022. 2023 and 2024 bad debts ($9,000 and $12,000) are ordinary small write-offs. The $22,000 is treated as non-recurring; the $16,000 excess above the 2023-2024 average of $10,500 is added back.

positive.title: Improving profitability and margins
positive.detail: EBITDA grew 76% from $875,000 in 2021 to $1,537,000 in 2024. Adjusted EBITDA margin improved from 11.4% to 15.7%. SDE margin improved from 13.5% to 17.3%. Gross margin stable at 28.7%-30.0%. (Check: the normalization computes 2024 adjusted EBITDA as $1,552,000, not $1,537,000.)

neutral.title: Dividends paid to owner are not add-backs
neutral.detail: Class D dividends of $60,000 paid in 2024 (and 2023) to Gord McAllister are distributions of after-tax profit from retained earnings. They do not appear on the P&L and are not add-backs to EBITDA or SDE. Seller's claimed owner compensation of $260,000 appears to include dividends, but only the salary ($180,000) is an add-back.

ownerCompDiscrepancy.interviewValue: $260,000 total owner compensation — Seller's add-back list (email June 3, 2025)
ownerCompDiscrepancy.documentValue: $180,000 T4 salary (management salary to shareholder Gord McAllister) — T2 corporate tax return 2024 and compiled financial statements FY2024
ownerCompDiscrepancy.explanation: The seller's add-back list claims $260,000 total owner compensation. However, the T2 tax return and compiled financial statements show only $180,000 in management salary (T4 employment income) paid to Gord McAllister. The T5 shows $60,000 in dividends (Class D shares), and the seller's add-back list also includes $28,000 in personal expenses (truck, fuel, insurance, meals, cell, season tickets). However, dividends are NOT an expense on the P&L and cannot be added back to EBITDA or SDE. Only the salary ($180,000) is an add-back for owner compensation. Personal expenses ($28,000) are a separate discretionary add-back. The seller's $260,000 figure is incorrect because it includes dividends, which are distributions of after-tax profit from retained earnings, not an expense.
ownerCompDiscrepancy.suggestedResolution: Explain that dividends are not an expense on the P&L and cannot be added back to EBITDA or SDE. The correct owner compensation add-back is $180,000 (T4 salary). Personal expenses ($28,000) are a separate discretionary add-back. Update the seller's understanding and the add-back list to reflect the correct treatment. For CIM purposes, use $180,000 as the owner compensation add-back and $28,000 as a separate discretionary add-back for personal expenses.
